title: One Sequential Recommendation Model Pretrained from Synthetic Priors Predicts Multiple Datasets

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation models are trained using dataset-specific item catalogs and interaction distributions.

gap.claim: Dataset-specific training limits generalization to new domains and typically requires retraining from scratch.

contributions.claim: SRPFN predicts the next item in a single forward pass without gradient-based parameter updates in the target domain.
SRPFN is pretrained offline on 25.6M synthetic sequences spanning diverse item-to-item transition patterns to produce posterior predictive next-item distributions.
At inference time, SRPFN conditions on target-domain item-item transition examples to adapt without retraining.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SRPFN achieves the best or second-best performance across nearly all metrics and datasets in experiments on five benchmarks against 10 baselines.
The authors report that SRPFN is substantially more computationally efficient than trained baselines.
The authors report that a single model pretrained on synthetic priors generalizes across diverse real-world domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing sequential recommendation models depend on dataset-specific training tied to the catalog and interaction distribution.
Generalization to new domains is limited because retraining from scratch is typically required.
SRPFN performs next-item prediction in one forward pass without target-domain gradient updates.
The model is pretrained on synthetic transition-pattern sequences and adapts through target-domain transition examples at inference.
The authors report strong benchmark performance, computational efficiency, and cross-domain generalization.

source_observation.claim: A model pretrained on a synthetic prior can condition on target-domain examples to produce recommendations without parameter updates.

interpretation.claim: In-context adaptation may reduce the need for domain-specific retraining when the prior captures relevant transition-pattern diversity.

application.claim: This approach could be considered for recommendation settings where rapid deployment across new domains is important.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how performance depends on the synthetic prior or the target-domain support set.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark names or metric values.
The abstract does not describe the synthetic prior generation procedure.
The abstract does not specify the size or composition of the target-domain support set.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols or statistical uncertainty.
